name: Skeleton of Thought
description: Skeleton of Thought is a two-phase generation strategy that separates structural planning from detailed writing. In the first phase, the model produces a concise numbered skeleton of up to max_points distinct logically ordered points without filling in details, serving as a scaffold that guarantees coverage of all required topics before any prose is written. In the second phase, the model expands each skeleton point independently into polished self-contained prose, focusing only on the assigned point. This decomposition makes the strategy ideal for long-form content generation — reports, articles, documentation, and educational material — where structural coherence across sections is critical. Because each point is expanded in isolation, the approach also enables parallel execution across multiple model calls. The final output is assembled from the individually expanded points to produce a complete document with clear logical flow.

prompts.skeleton_prompt: Create a concise numbered skeleton for answering the task by identifying the key topics that must be covered in the final response. Use no more than {max_points} points so the skeleton remains focused and each point represents a meaningful section rather than a trivial detail. Make each point distinct and ordered logically so that the sequence builds toward a coherent conclusion, with earlier points establishing context for later ones. Do not fill in the details yet — each point should be a short label or phrase that marks what will be expanded, not the expansion itself. Keep every point short enough to guide a later expansion without constraining the writer to a specific phrasing or angle. Ensure the skeleton covers the full scope of the task, leaving no required topic unrepresented. Return only the numbered skeleton, with no commentary, no partial expansions, and no justification for the chosen structure.
prompts.expand_prompt: Complete this one skeleton point for the original task by expanding it into polished, self-contained prose that a reader could understand without seeing the other points. Stay focused on the provided point — do not drift into adjacent topics or try to cover material assigned to other skeleton entries. Add the facts, reasoning, and examples needed for that point to stand alone as a complete subsection of the final document. Do not rewrite unrelated skeleton points or attempt to synthesize the full answer, since those points will be expanded separately and assembled later. Keep the expansion coherent with the full task by referencing the original prompt scope and constraints where relevant, but without duplicating the material of other points. Maintain a consistent tone and style suitable for the target audience implied by the task. Return polished prose for this point only, with no preamble, no closing filler, and no cross-references to other skeleton entries.
